title: Congress Says MeitY Blocked Rahul Gandhi's Instagram Posts
excerpt: Viral posts from Vijay's Tamil Nadu swearing-in vanished briefly — sparking a sharp clash over India's digital censorship powers.
body:
On May 10, 2026, Rahul Gandhi attended the swearing-in of actor-politician Vijay as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister — then watched his own viral posts from the ceremony disappear off Instagram without explanation.

**What happened:**
Congress claimed that Instagram had 'blocked' Gandhi's reel and photo post featuring him and actor-politician Vijay, attributing the action to rules of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The reel received 12 million views in under an hour, while the photo post had reached 46 million people — making the sudden disappearance all the more striking. Congress leader Srivatsa argued, 'This is how India's opposition leader's voice is curtailed.'

**The government's pushback:**
MeitY denied any involvement in the blocking, clarifying that the ministry had nothing to do with the action taken by the social media platform. Sources confirmed the blocking resulted from Instagram's own internal mechanisms, which mistakenly flagged Gandhi's posts for removal, and that the content has since been restored. Meta, which owns Instagram, cited no reason as to why his account became inaccessible for a time.

**Why the timing matters:**
Transparency reporting from Meta indicates an exponential increase in content restricted on Instagram and Facebook in India in response to government orders for each reporting period between January 2024 and December 2025. Under the Modi administration, blocking requests have rapidly increased from 6,000 annually in January 2018 to 12,600 in 2024, and nearly doubled again to 24,300 in 2025. That backdrop gives Congress's accusations — however disputed — an uncomfortable plausibility.

**What to watch:**
Whether Meta issues a formal explanation for the outage will determine whether this episode fades as a glitch or hardens into a sustained campaign over digital freedoms ahead of the next electoral cycle.
